messages:
emily_cs: Heads-up — ACME (acct: acme-prod) just opened a P1 ticket: sustained 429s for ~6m during their morning ramp. They claim dedicated pool didn't scale; they saw requests queueing and auth attach failures in client logs. I linked the ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/4321 :eyes:

jake_support: Ack. Can you paste the key logs or repro steps? Do we have request timestamps and sample request IDs? Any customer-visible errors besides 429?

emily_cs: They reported two patterns: (1) immediate 429s from our API layer, (2) intermittent `attach heartbeat` failures in worker logs with `403` from IAM during account token rotation. Customer says they saw a spike from 180rps -> 900rps and expected autoscale to add nodes.

ryan_eng-runtime: Thanks — a few quick checks to run while we triage: 1) confirm minReplica for their dedicated pool; 2) check warm-pool usage and probe pacing; 3) look for registry/imagepull backoffs. From similar incidents, token rotation causing attach auth failures can stall the warm chain and block scaleup.

sasha_eng-platform: Emily/Jake — I pulled infra logs for acme-prod: we saw probe throttling around 08:04-08:09 UTC and a short IAM 429/403 burst at 08:05:12. Relevant excerpt:

```
2026-03-17T08:05:12Z attach-controller ERROR attach failed: 403 token rotated for account acme-prod
2026-03-17T08:05:13Z warmpool-prober WARN probe suppressed due to rate-limit
2026-03-17T08:05:15Z autoscaler INFO desired=20 current=8 minReplica=8 maxReplica=200
2026-03-17T08:06:20Z scale-trigger queued but warmpool depleted
```

sasha_eng-platform: Looks like minReplica==8, warmpool was at 0, and the autoscaler attempted to scale but probes were suppressed for a short window while IAM rotation churned tokens. That lines up with 6m of degraded capacity while the system recovered.

jake_support: Customer also mentioned billing/account rotation earlier this week — could that have affected IAM calls?

ryan_eng-runtime: Yes — if credential rotation ran concurrently and resulted in transient 403s, attach attempts will fail and the warm provisioning path can fall back to slower cold starts. Two mitigations: 1) short-term: increase burst capacity or manually spin warm nodes for them, 2) medium-term: add probe backoff jitter to avoid global probe suppression.

infra_bot: Runbook reminder: run `rdwctl pool warm --account acme-prod --count 12` to seed warm pool (requires support role). See: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/warmpool#manual-seed

emily_cs: I'm going to offer manual warm-seed and a short config change to customer. Proposed message: "We've seeded warm capacity and opened an engineering investigation; recommend bumping minReplica from 8 -> 12 for morning ramp windows while we root cause." OK? :thumbsup:

sasha_eng-platform: +1. Also will open a platform PR to improve probe suppression heuristics and add observability to detect when token rotation coincides with scale actions.

ryan_eng-runtime: I'll own post-mortem: repro steps, add a regression test where IAM rotation sim is run during ramp, and validate autoscaler fallback isn't blocked by attach auth failures.

jake_support: I'm drafting the customer update. Will note: manual warm seed done, temporary minReplica bump suggested, engineering investigating for root cause and regression fix. ETA for next update 30m.

emily_cs: Thanks team. I'll update ACME now and mark ticket P1. tagging oncall for follow-through: @ryan_eng-runtime please escalate to eng-sre if you hit resource quota or noisy neighbor findings. :white_check_mark:
